status_summary: A trade publication reported on 2025-03-14, and an April 2025 working paper of the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network placed at the 58th plenary meeting of the General Assembly in March 2025, a US statement rejecting the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals; a mailing-list post quoting the remarks dates them to 2025-03-04, and the US Mission's own text could not be opened. A presidential memorandum signed 2026-01-07 (91 FR 2281, published 2026-01-16) directs withdrawal from 35 non-UN organizations and 31 UN entities, including UN DESA, UN-Habitat, the UN-REDD programme, the International Tropical Timber Organization and the International Cotton Advisory Committee, but names none of FAO, IFAD, WFP, the Committee on World Food Security or the UN Food Systems Summit, and does not mention the 2030 Agenda. The Hub's report on the July 2025 Food Systems Summit stocktake in Addis Ababa does not mention the United States, and a USDA page endorsing the Summit's goals remained readable on 2026-10-12. The general position against the 2030 Agenda and the withdrawal from UN DESA are partly operative, but no food-specific disengagement was found, so the record is in_progress at 25.

timeline.event: At the 58th plenary meeting of the General Assembly, the US Minister Counselor to ECOSOC states that the United States rejects the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals (date from a mailing-list post of 2025-03-07 quoting the remarks; a trade publication reported the statement on 2025-03-14 and an SDSN working paper places it in March 2025; the US Mission text was not opened).
The second UN Food Systems Summit stocktake (UNFSS+4) concluded in Addis Ababa; the Hub's report does not mention US participation.

A CRS report stated that the FY2026 request for Contributions to International Organizations was $263.8 million, about 83 percent below the FY2025 pre-rescission level, and that the US had begun withdrawal from WHO and left UNESCO.

A presidential memorandum directed withdrawal from 66 organizations, including UN-Habitat, the International Tropical Timber Organization and the UN-REDD programme; FAO, IFAD and WFP are not among those listed.

title: Remove the U.S. from UN-linked sustainable-development efforts tied to food production
uncertainties: The US Mission remarks page could not be fetched; the statement rejecting the 2030 Agenda rests on a trade publication, an SDSN working paper (an advocacy-research body) and a mailing-list post that quotes the remarks and dates them to 2025-03-04, which agree on its substance. The memorandum of 2026-01-07 was read in full on the Federal Register; it sets no deadlines, is subject to law and appropriations, and names no food or agriculture body other than the International Cotton Advisory Committee and the International Tropical Timber Organization. The US role at the July 2025 stocktake was searched and not found. No data on current US funding to FAO, IFAD or WFP were found; the CRS note says the account that traditionally funded voluntary contributions such as WFP's was zeroed in July 2025 and that funding through other accounts is unclear. The USDA 2021 food systems page carries no update date. Whether the withdrawals are intended to reach food production schemes is not stated in the sources. The general withdrawal is covered by c06-03. The SDSN paper is dated April 2025 without a day; 2025-04-01 is a placeholder date.
